result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both are focused intake forms with instrument-specific fields. In what is visible, B gives more help where customers are likely to get stuck: it explains why contact details are needed, gives friendlier placeholders and shows problem options that change with the chosen instrument. A is solid but asks for more, such as a serial number and a preferred contact method. Neither screenshot shows the confirmation, so item 3 is scored conservatively for both. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Only the top of each form is visible, so I couldn't judge either confirmation screen (item 3 is scored neutrally for both). Both are focused intake forms with instrument-specific wording. A gives more help where customers might get stuck: it explains why contact details are needed, offers a make/model example like "old German violin", and shows common problems for whichever instrument is chosen. B adds fields the repairer may not need, such as "Best way to reach you" next to the phone and email fields, and its "Instrument only" checkbox can be ticked alongside "Case", which contradicts itself.
